correctness.rationale: At common \(N,P\), \(F_1=2TP/(P+TP+FP)\) and balanced accuracy is \(\frac12(1+TP/P-FP/(N-P))\). Every strictly positive matrix is enumerated exactly. There is no strict reversal through \(N=6\), one weak-only split at \(N=6\), and exactly three strict reversals at \(N=7\).

evidence: Balanced accuracy is the mean of sensitivity and specificity.
For binary classification, Youden Informedness is sensitivity plus specificity minus one, so balanced accuracy is affine-equivalent to Informedness.

originality.rationale: Prior literature establishes generic F-measure versus Informedness disagreement, so novelty is restricted to the exact fixed-prevalence positive-cell finite boundary and complete first layer. The checked literature, exact-matrix searches, database searches, and own-ledger comparisons did not state or imply that boundary.
residual_risks: Generic F1-versus-Informedness disagreement is known; originality is limited to the exact fixed-prevalence positive-cell finite cutoff and complete first layer.

value.rationale: F1 and balanced accuracy are widely used classifier summaries with different treatment of the negative class. By fixing both prevalence and sample size and excluding zero-cell degeneracies, the theorem isolates the smallest genuinely nontrivial data set where metric choice alone reverses model preference, and it classifies every minimal reversal.
